title: Rabies Needs Proof, Quarantine, and Dog-Trade Abolition by 2030
excerpt: Rabies kills after symptoms appear. Unverified “tradition” and “farm-raised” claims cannot excuse weak quarantine, opaque transport, or stolen-pet risk.
body_html:
Rabies gives families no second chance: once clinical symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. World Health Organization guidance requires immediate wound washing and urgent medical assessment after possible exposure. This public-health reality leaves no room for secret transport, uninspected slaughter, or unsupported claims about how animals entered trade.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

“Tradition” proves no lawful origin. “Farm-raised” proves nothing without licensed facilities, animal identification, veterinary records, transport documents, and quarantine compliance. Without those records, consumers and families cannot distinguish legally sourced animals from stolen companions or animals moved outside disease-control systems.

Pet theft is not cultural debate. It is a crime against families. Operators who steal dogs destroy trust, inflict grief, and turn companion animals into anonymous cargo. Any confirmed theft deserves police investigation, prosecution, and restitution. Any claim about a specific syndicate, conviction, seizure, or poison-bait incident needs a public court or agency record. No such record is identified here, so no invented raid, victim, or verdict belongs in this campaign.

Biosecurity cannot stop at household gates

Household rabies exposure and commercial supply-chain risk are parallel failures, not proof that one caused the other. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route.

Vietnamese families, veterinarians, public-health workers, and animal-protection advocates can demand stronger records, quarantine enforcement, transport controls, and protection for companion animals. State health targets are not the same as SDE’s policy demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Replace legal gaps with public protection

Sign SDE’s national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
